title: The Composite Self: A Dynamical Model of Semantic States and Relational Topology
content: Can the organization of a person's relational roles change while the strengths of those roles stay fixed? We model role strengths as signed weights, project them into a semantic space, and track connected components in a filtration of the weighted role graph. When all surviving intervals are closed at zero, the longest interval equals the largest absolute role weight for every edge configuration. To isolate edge sensitivity, we exchanged edges in 480 synthetic networks while preserving each role's amplitude, degree, and connected component. The remaining intervals changed in 479 networks at two-decimal resolution. In a separate two-dimensional reduction, increasing the strength of prior anchoring produces a local supercritical pitchfork. Comparisons on held-out synthetic data show that the predictive value of a coordinate decomposition depends on the generating process. Together these results distinguish changes in relational strength from changes in organization. Testing whether the latter predicts perceived self-continuity requires a continuity measure collected independently of the role graph.
